title: GitHub Trending Summary - Weekly - 2026-11-20
ranking_explanation: Repositories are ordered by the weekly star-gain values displayed on GitHub Trending at snapshot time; current total stars and default-branch commit SHAs were corroborated via GitHub REST API.
global_caveat: Trending and star-gain figures are a point-in-time GitHub view, not a measure of usage, quality, or long-term adoption. No prior-week comparison is claimed.

sources.corroboration: Unauthenticated GitHub REST API: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo} and GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{default_branch}; checked for all 13 repositories.

themes.title: Agent workflow infrastructure
themes.content: Office editing, human review, code review, and app-connection protocols are emerging as a substantial layer around coding agents.

themes.title: Agent context and skills
themes.content: Projects package expert knowledge and task-specific capabilities as reusable context or skills for agents.

themes.title: Browser and UI tooling
themes.content: The trend spans browser inspection and automation, agent-ready design systems, and office-style interfaces.

themes.title: Focused end-user utilities
themes.content: A smaller non-agent segment includes personal finance software and a platform-specific Apple Watch utility.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time: 2026-11-20 02:43 UTC. Scope: Weekly. Date range: 2026-11-13 through 2026-11-20 (rolling seven-day view). Ranking basis: GitHub Trending weekly star gains, corroborated against GitHub REST repository and commit data.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent-oriented software is the clearest shared current: the largest weekly gains went to an AI office SDK and web guidance for coding agents, while code review, browser control, agent interfaces, and human review surfaces fill out the list. The spread suggests momentum is moving from agent models alone toward the tools and interfaces that make agent work usable and reviewable.

sections.title: dream-num/univer
sections.description: An extensible office SDK for embedding spreadsheets, documents, collaboration, and file processing in products and agent workflows.
sections.why_notable: It led this snapshot's star gains, reflecting strong interest in making office-style editing and collaboration programmable for agents.

sections.title: GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src
sections.description: Source for skills that put modern web platform best practices and browser compatibility guidance into coding agents.
sections.why_notable: It was the second-largest weekly gainer and directly targets a common weakness in generated code: reliance on outdated web patterns.

sections.title: meta/astryx
sections.description: Meta's customizable React design system, built on React 19 and StyleX and intended for people and coding agents.
sections.why_notable: A mature design system entering the open-source agent-ready UI space drew a large weekly gain.
sections.unique_caveat: The README labels the project beta.

sections.title: alibaba/open-code-review
sections.description: A code-review CLI combining deterministic checks with an LLM agent and line-level feedback.
sections.why_notable: Its strong gain points to interest in constrained, reviewable agent workflows rather than unconstrained code generation alone.

sections.title: backnotprop/plannotator
sections.description: A local browser-based surface for annotating agent plans, documents, artifacts, and code reviews, then returning feedback to agents.
sections.why_notable: It exemplifies the growing human-in-the-loop layer around multi-agent and coding-agent work.

sections.title: ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui
sections.description: An event-based protocol for connecting AI agents to user-facing applications.
sections.why_notable: Its stable protocol and SDK approach address integration across different agent frameworks and frontend clients.

sections.title: tradermonty/claude-trading-skills
sections.description: Claude Code skills for investment research, charting, screeners, calendars, and trading workflows.
sections.why_notable: It shows agent skill bundles branching into a specific professional domain rather than remaining general-purpose.

sections.title: ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp
sections.description: An MCP server and CLI giving coding agents live Chrome automation, debugging, and performance-inspection capabilities.
sections.why_notable: It brings agents closer to the browser runtime and its diagnostics, not just source code.
sections.unique_caveat: The project warns that MCP clients can inspect and modify data in the controlled browser; use a browser instance without sensitive information.

sections.title: we-promise/sure
sections.description: A self-hostable personal-finance and wealth-management application.
sections.why_notable: It is a notable non-agent-specific product among an otherwise agent-heavy group.
sections.unique_caveat: The maintainers describe it as a community fork of the archived Maybe Finance project.

sections.title: mvanhorn/last30days-skill
sections.description: An agent skill that researches a topic across social platforms and web sources, then synthesizes a grounded summary.
sections.why_notable: The gain reflects appetite for repeatable, multi-source research workflows packaged for agents.

sections.title: kajisho5/ffmpeg-skill
sections.description: A local video-editing skill for coding agents, exposing FFmpeg operations through tools and an MCP server.
sections.why_notable: It extends agent workflows into practical media editing while emphasizing local execution.

sections.title: google-labs-code/stitch-skills
sections.description: A library of agent skills for Google's Stitch MCP server, designed for compatibility across several coding agents.
sections.why_notable: It reflects the rise of portable, standards-oriented skill bundles and MCP-connected design workflows.

sections.title: pookjw/HermesEnabler
sections.description: A tool for enabling Hermès watch faces on Apple Watch devices.
sections.why_notable: It is a platform-specific utility that provides a useful counterpoint to the dominant agent and developer-tool themes.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent workflow infrastructure includes office tooling, human review, code review, and agent-to-app protocols (Univer, Open Code Review, Plannotator, AG-UI). Agent context and skills package domain knowledge or capabilities (Modern Web Guidance, Claude Trading Skills, Last30Days Skill, FFmpeg Skill, Stitch Skills). Browser and UI tooling includes Chrome DevTools MCP, Astryx, and Univer. TypeScript appears in 7 of 13 repositories, Python in 3, and Go, Ruby, and Objective-C in 1 each.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: This week's strongest signal is an expanding agent tooling layer: guidance, skills, browser access, human review, app protocols, and editable office environments all attracted substantial gains. At the same time, Sure and HermesEnabler show that focused end-user utilities still find an audience outside the AI-agent wave.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary source: https://github.com/trending?since=weekly, read at 2026-11-20 02:43 UTC. Star gains and displayed total stars are from that page. Corroboration: unauthenticated GitHub REST API repository and default-branch commit endpoints checked for all 13 entries. Ranked by weekly star gains shown on GitHub Trending; no prior-week comparison is asserted.
